signals.observation: Explicit downward movement into the Piraeus opens the narration.
Forms of θεάομαι frame the section: first as Socrates' stated purpose for descending, then as Polemarchus' inducement to stay; θεωρέω appears between them for the completed viewing of the procession.

elements.context: ἐκέλευσε δραμόντα τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ κελεῦσαι

signals.observation: περιμένω recurs four times in rapid succession, passing from Polemarchus' command through the slave to Socrates and Glaucon's compliance.

elements.context: τὸ ἢν πείσωμεν ὑμᾶς ὡς χρὴ ἡμᾶς ἀφεῖναι
ἦ καὶ δύναισθ᾽ ἄν, ἦ δ᾽ ὅς, πεῖσαι μὴ ἀκούοντας

signals.observation: Socrates proposes persuading (πείσωμεν) as the remaining option; Polemarchus immediately blocks it with the condition μὴ ἀκούοντας, making persuasion impossible.

elements.context: κατιδὼν οὖν πόρρωθεν ἡμᾶς οἴκαδε ὡρμημένους
ᾖμεν οὖν οἴκαδε εἰς τοῦ Πολεμάρχου

signals.observation: οἴκαδε first describes Socrates heading toward his own home; it returns naming arrival at Polemarchus' house instead.
πρὸς τὸ ἄστυ marks the intended direction of departure; πρὸς ἑσπέραν marks the time-direction of the evening event that prevents it.

elements.context: ἐκέλευσε δραμόντα τὸν παῖδα περιμεῖναί ἑ κελεῦσαι

elements.form: ὄπισθεν ὁ παῖς λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου

signals.observation: The slave (παῖς) runs forward at Polemarchus' command, then physically grasps Socrates' cloak from behind—a bodily detention.

elements.context: καλὴ μὲν οὖν μοι καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐπιχωρίων πομπὴ ἔδοξεν εἶναι
οὐ μέντοι ἧττον ἐφαίνετο πρέπειν ἣν οἱ Θρᾷκες ἔπεμπον

signals.observation: The local procession is judged beautiful but the Thracian procession appears no less fitting—a comparison between native and foreign elements.
The festival is explicitly being held for the first time (νῦν πρῶτον).
μένω appears alongside περιμένω as Polemarchus' demand; Glaucon's μενετέον (verbal adjective of necessity) marks the yielding.

elements.form: ὁράτε οὖν ἡμᾶς, ἔφη, ὅσοι ἐσμέν

signals.observation: Polemarchus draws attention to numerical superiority (ὅσοι ἐσμέν) as the ground for the constraint on Socrates.

elements.context: καθῆστο δὲ ἐστεφανωμένος ἐπί τινος προσκεφαλαίου τε καὶ δίφρου
τεθυκὼς γὰρ ἐτύγχανεν ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ

signals.observation: Cephalus is found crowned and seated, having just sacrificed in the courtyard—ritual state upon arrival.

elements.context: καὶ συνεσόμεθά τε πολλοῖς τῶν νέων

signals.observation: Polemarchus projects a sequence of future activities in first-person plural: rising after dinner, viewing the pannychis, being with the young men, and conversing (διαλεξόμεθα).

elements.form: λαμπάδια ἔχοντες διαδώσουσιν ἀλλήλοις ἁμιλλώμενοι τοῖς ἵπποις

signals.observation: The torch-relay on horseback (λαμπάδια + ἵπποις) is called καινόν by Socrates—something novel and unexpected.

elements.form: ἐκαθεζόμεθα οὖν παρ᾽ αὐτόν· ἔκειντο γὰρ δίφροι τινὲς αὐτόθι κύκλῳ

signals.observation: The section closes with the group sitting in a circle (κύκλῳ) of chairs around Cephalus.
